clue.text: Show tunes?

parts.note: a stage show's songs, taken together, are what its title names: a famous Rodgers and Hammerstein musical about the von Trapp family

explanation.surface: A plain request or heading: the songs from a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a category of songs; the question mark says to take 'tunes' as all the notes heard together, which is the title of the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the musical literally describes what tunes are: audible melody, so the show's name fits a description of its own songs.

clue.text: International ship president promoted alongside one produced artificially?

parts.note: a test match is an international cricket or rugby fixture
a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved upwards, so the president's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
by means beside or alongside

explanation.surface: A news item about an international ship and a president being promoted beside someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns ABE upward into EBA, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A child conceived by in-vitro fertilisation is popularly described as made in laboratory glassware, i.e. produced artificially.

clue.text: Mysterious English lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A description of an English lake shrouded in mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something strange and uncanny is mysterious.

clue.text: Subject of 'Operation Iron' dumped on journalist

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces are placed on top of the journalist

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a crackdown codenamed 'Operation Iron' being heaped on a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' is an adjective here, as in a subject people under a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a people kept in subjection under harsh rule are subject or downtrodden.

clue.text: Oil container lifted — hot that, mostly!

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the container's letters are read upward

parts.note: a pan is a cooking container
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word that, its final letter lost

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a hot oil container being raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns PAN into NAP; 'mostly' trims THAT to THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable oil distilled from petroleum or coal tar.

clue.text: Caucasus area's a site so varied

indicators.note: varied means the letters of a site so are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: A travel note: a Caucasus region is a site so diverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the region split between North Ossetia in Russia and South Ossetia lies in the Caucasus mountains.

clue.text: Maiden with a song in 1ac?

parts.note: M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
an aria is a song for solo voice

explanation.surface: A question about which young woman sings in the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the heroine of the musical is a young novice who sings, and a song about her bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The governess heroine of the musical, played on screen by Julie Andrews, is a maiden with songs.

clue.text: Pinch my half of sofa in clash related to 1ac?

indicators.note: in clash means the letters are jumbled as if in conflict
half of takes the first two of the four letters of sofa

explanation.surface: Someone squeezed onto half a sofa during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives SO, which joins PINCHMY; 'in clash' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or like a symphony, an orchestral form, hence relating to music.

clue.text: Tear off from furthest Ripon

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words furthest Ripon

explanation.surface: An instruction to tear something off at the far end of Ripon, a Yorkshire cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tear off a covering or layer is to peel it away.

clue.text: Beef about transport being Dad's first bit of indignation

indicators.note: first says the dad's piece comes before the transport

parts.note: pa is dad, keeping the possessive S
a tram is a form of public transport

indicators.note: bit of takes only the opening letter of indignation

explanation.surface: A grumble about transport stirring Dad's first flash of indignation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'being' are only links. 'first' places PA'S ahead of TRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a highly seasoned smoked beef, often served in sandwiches.

clue.text: Bored nude modelled without gain …

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram goes around the gain
modelled means the letters of nude are shaped into a new form

parts.note: interest is gain earned on money

explanation.surface: An art class where a nude sat for nothing and the model was bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside; 'modelled' makes UNED, which sits around the gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone bored shows no curiosity or engagement.

clue.text: Death rate falls — heartlessly, aid is withdrawn after that

indicators.note: falls is the anagram signal, the letters tumbling into a new order
is withdrawn says those outer letters are taken away from the shuffled pool
heartlessly drops the middle of aid, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A grim statistic: the death rate drops once aid is cruelly cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' makes AD from AID; 'is withdrawn' removes them from DEATH RATE, and 'falls' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adverb: an old word meaning thereupon, following on from that.

clue.text: Debate incorporates refreshment and a bit of jaw

parts.note: tea is a drink and also a light meal
the chin is the front part of the lower jaw

explanation.surface: A debate that includes a tea break and a bit of chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' and 'and' are links; 'jaw' looks like chat but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal debate or discussion session, originally a campus protest event in the 1960s.

clue.text: Squanders 1ac?

definitions.meaning: slang verb meaning blows or wastes money, from the old use of blue for spending recklessly
a genre of melancholy music from the American South

explanation.surface: A one-word charge against a spendthrift, with a nod to music.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a slang verb for frittering cash away, and a sorrowful African-American musical genre.

clue.text: … Greek character turned up with nothing and quietly modelled in open

indicators.note: turned up means read upward, as this is a down clue

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
O looks like zero, nothing
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
posed means sat as a model

explanation.surface: Continuing from 10-down: a Greek figure appeared with nothing on and modelled quietly in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes NU into UN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of an open goal or open field: without any resistance or opposition.

clue.text: King advanced, match starts to mean nothing's feasible

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level
a game is a match

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: on means possible or workable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A monarch moved forward, and the match began to look pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Greek king of Mycenae who led the expedition against Troy.

clue.text: Marsh's eastern edge, in which stableman gets trapped

definitions.note: Marsh's stands for marsh is, the noun then the link

indicators.note: gets trapped means the stableman goes inside the edge

parts.note: a verge is a border or edge
a lad is a stable hand at a racing yard

explanation.surface: A horse handler stuck at the east edge of a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is a link, the edge holding the stableman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tract of swampy grassland, as in the vast Florida wetland.

clue.text: Sticks may be advantage with crops

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or advantage
to dock is to cut short, as in cropping a tail

explanation.surface: A farming thought: sticks might help the crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' is the remote countryside, not twigs; 'crops' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the sticks and this American slang word both mean remote rural backwoods.

clue.text: Spot aircraftsman climbing over 1ac?

indicators.note: climbing means read upward, as this is a down clue

parts.note: to spot is to see or spy
LAC is a leading aircraftman in the RAF
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A spotter watching an airman scale a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses SPYLAC upward to CALYPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Caribbean style of song from Trinidad, a kind of music.

clue.text: Levers operated on time with little app

indicators.note: operated means the letters of levers are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Machine levers worked to a schedule using a small application.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small Java program running on a web server, a tiny application.

clue.text: Team's clever regularly to find anchorman

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of Team's clever

explanation.surface: A team's smart move to find its anchor in a relay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anchorman' looks like the last runner in a team; here it is a presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a master of ceremonies or show host, like a broadcast anchor.

clue.text: Bail out over outskirts of Poole, with spot of difficulty standing upright

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters spread across the other pieces, enclosing them
out means the letters of bail are thrown into disorder
outskirts of takes the first and last letters of Poole
spot of takes just the opening letter of difficulty

explanation.surface: A harbour crisis: bailing out near Poole, a Dorset coastal town, with some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bail out' looks like a phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal making BIAL; 'over' has it spread across the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for walking on two legs, which needs an upright stance.

clue.text: Amusing marionette's boxed right

indicators.note: boxed means the puppet's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a marionette is a puppet, a kind of doll; the possessive gives 'doll has'

explanation.surface: A puppet packed away in a box, just so.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drily or quaintly funny.

clue.text: College date for fundraising in 1ac

definitions.meaning: rag week is a British student charity event, so split 3,4 this names its period
a syncopated piano music style from turn-of-the-century America

explanation.surface: A student calendar entry for a charity fundraiser, set in music.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a British student charity fundraising stunt; split 3,4 the answer reads as the time for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a student charity season, and the syncopated piano genre of Scott Joplin.

clue.text: For seconds, fish, agreeably flavoured, lovingly cooked in house

indicators.note: For seconds says to take the second letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A cook going back for seconds of fish, tasty and lovingly prepared at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like second helpings, but means second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Inuit dome-shaped dwelling built of snow blocks.

clue.text: Agitated townspeople denied personal legal principle

indicators.note: agitated means the letters of townspeople are stirred into a new order
denied says the letters for personal are taken away from the pool

parts.note: own means personal, as in one's own

explanation.surface: Angry locals refused something private under a point of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' takes OWN from TOWNSPEOPLE; 'Agitated' shuffles the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term: a rule preventing someone from going back on an earlier statement or act.

clue.text: Dispense with every book

parts.note: all means every one
OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand out a copy with every book.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to share out or distribute portions.

clue.text: Where cats' eyes shine for 1ac?

definitions.meaning: cats' eyes are British reflective road studs set along the centre line of a road
a style of bland, easy-listening popular music

explanation.surface: Where a cat's eyes glint at night, and a kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats' eyes are reflective studs set in British roads, not an animal's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the centre line of a highway, and a mainstream, inoffensive kind of music.
